issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation omits the phrase 'μη αποθανη' (so that they may not die) and replaces it with a conditional 'để ai ăn nó thì không chết' (so that whoever eats it does not die). The Greek implies a purpose/result for those who eat, but the Vietnamese structure changes the logical relationship to a conditional result.

The Greek 'ινα τις εξ αυτου φαγη' means 'so that they [the people] may eat from it'. The Vietnamese 'để ai ăn nó' changes the subject from a general group ('they') to an indefinite pronoun ('whoever').
